Anemia_and_Transfusion.Summary: No established strategy for treating anaemia in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Efficacy and safety of blood transfusion in this scenario remains unknown.
Anemia_and_Transfusion.Transfusion_Strategies_and_Definitions: In most studies: liberal transfusion defined approximately as any red blood cell transfusion at haemoglobin ≈<10 g/dL; restrictive transfusion defined approximately as any transfusion at haemoglobin ≈<8 g/dL.
Anemia_and_Transfusion.Observational_Data: Observational data suggest liberal transfusion may be associated with increased all-cause mortality.
Anemia_and_Transfusion.REALITY_Trial: Open-label trial (REALITY) randomized 668 ACS patients to restrictive (triggered by haemoglobin ~8 g/dL) vs liberal (~10 g/dL). At 30 days composite outcome (all-cause death, stroke, recurrent MI, or emergency revascularization) comparable between arms (11% vs 14%, RR 0.79) meeting pre-specified non-inferiority; however all components were numerically higher in liberal arm. 1-year follow-up yielded contradictory conclusions: restrictive strategy did not achieve non-inferiority for MACE vs liberal, and a post-hoc analysis showed increased risk in the restrictive group between day 30 and 1 year.
Anemia_and_Transfusion.Recommendation: Therefore, no formal recommendation as to the optimal transfusion strategy (liberal vs restrictive) in ACS can be made at present.

Thrombocytopenia.Summary: Clinically relevant thrombocytopaenia in ACS defined and consequences.
Thrombocytopenia.Definitions: Clinically relevant thrombocytopaenia: platelet count <100,000/µL or a relative drop in platelet count of 50% from baseline in the context of ACS.
Thrombocytopenia.Risks: Thrombocytopaenia increases risk of death, major bleeding events, and life-threatening thrombotic events.
Thrombocytopenia.ARC-HBR: ARC-HBR criteria define platelet count <100,000/µL as a major criterion for high bleeding risk (HBR).
Thrombocytopenia.Management_Note: Management of GP IIb/IIIa inhibitor- and heparin-induced thrombocytopaenia is discussed in the supplementary data online.

Chronic_Kidney_Disease_(12.3.2).Summary: Moderate to severe chronic kidney disease (CKD stages IIIa–V) present in >30% of ACS patients and associated with worse prognosis.
Chronic_Kidney_Disease_(12.3.2).Impact_on_Care: Patients with ACS and concomitant CKD receive less interventional and pharmacological treatment and have worse prognosis than patients with normal kidney function.
Chronic_Kidney_Disease_(12.3.2).Contributing_Factors: Worse prognosis likely due to larger number of comorbidities and increased risk of in-hospital complications including serious bleeding.
Chronic_Kidney_Disease_(12.3.2).Evidence_on_Revascularization: Observational and registry-based data indicate ACS patients with moderate to severe CKD have a better prognosis with early revascularization than with medical therapy alone (RCT evidence lacking).
Chronic_Kidney_Disease_(12.3.2).Antithrombotic_and_Contrast_Consideratio: Type and dose of antithrombotic agent and the amount of contrast agent should be considered based on kidney function (see supplementary data, Table S15). Evidence regarding choice, timing and duration of i.v. hydration during/after revascularization is discussed further in the guideline.
